title: Men of Tattoos
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Loosely linked stories about three tattooed men in the yakuza underworld, Peony Katagi, Buttercup Mutou and Mad Shark Nogami, each tied to the mysterious Kubota, ending with a new chapter, 'Everyone's Song', about dreams that do not come true (AniList; MangaUpdates; Manga Bookshelf review). Two extra stories follow, one about a man visited nightly by the vengeful spirit of the man he loves, and a lighter pair about college students dreaming of each other. Rated Mature (18+) by Juné.
life_message: It asks whether men living on society's underside can find love or salvation, and often answers with loss (to verify).

content.note: Yakuza revenge stories (Manga Bookshelf); murder, violence and prison (MangaUpdates).
Tragedy, dead lovers, HIV/AIDS, a vengeful spirit (AniList Tragedy; MangaUpdates; blurb).

18+ rating and 'steamy' scenes (Manga Bookshelf); MangaDex rates it erotica; MangaUpdates lists rape, gang rape, sexual violence and an ero-guro label. Characters are adults (yakuza; college students).
Grief and despair; unfulfilled dreams (Manga Bookshelf).
Gang life and tattoos as identity (blurb).

dominant: Yakuza loyalty and revenge, tragic love, longing for salvation

frames.aligns: The stories ask about salvation for men on the margins (blurb).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Revenge stories in the yakuza world (Manga Bookshelf).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Boss's son and mid-ranking member (Manga Bookshelf).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Tattoo and gang codes; vengeful spirit folklore.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Hard lives and dreams that don't come true (review).

folkways.japan: Draws on Japanese yakuza codes of rank and loyalty, irezumi tattoos, and onryo (vengeful spirit) folklore.

delivery.evidence: Reviewer calls the storytelling clever and the book 'strange, funny, heartbreaking and surreal' (Manga Bookshelf, quoting Deb Aoki).
delivery.note: Themes come through tragic outcomes rather than statements.

winners_losers: Most yakuza characters' dreams go unfulfilled; the closing college-student stories end happily (Manga Bookshelf).
